title: One strip of squares scanned by a moving reader
summary: Pairs are written on a strip of 2C + 2 squares, address then item, after the last used square. To fetch, a reader moves from the first square two squares at a time until it sits on the wanted address and reads the next square. Removal blanks the pair. A three-mode controller decides what is written and read.
core_idea: Write pairs end to end on a strip and fetch by moving a reader along it, under a searched three-mode controller.

state.name: Sq
state.meaning: The strip: squares holding addresses and items in alternation, -1 when blank.

state.name: hd
state.meaning: Position of the reader on the strip.

state.name: en
state.meaning: First square after the last written pair.

state.name: ctl
state.meaning: Routing registers (mode, stop symbol sigma, hop limit H) and bookkeeping (pending p, flag w, position c, output count o, depth d), with the learned lists Z and A.

state.name: M
state.meaning: Learned translation from a read result to an emitted symbol, at most N entries for an alphabet of N symbols.

update.latex:
x_t=\sigma \Rightarrow w\leftarrow 0,\, o\leftarrow 0;\quad \mu=0:\; x_t\in Z \Rightarrow p\leftarrow\varnothing;\; w=1,\, p=\varnothing \Rightarrow p\leftarrow x_t;\; w=1,\, p
eq\varnothing \Rightarrow \mathrm{ins}(p, x_t),\, p\leftarrow\varnothing;\quad \mu=1:\; w=1,\, x_t
otin Z \Rightarrow \mathrm{ins}(c, x_t),\, c\leftarrow c+1;\; w=0 \Rightarrow o\leftarrow o+1;\quad \mu=2:\; x_t\in A \Rightarrow \mathrm{del}(d, \mathrm{get}(d)),\, d\leftarrow d-1;\; x_t
otin A \Rightarrow d\leftarrow d+1,\, \mathrm{ins}(d, x_t)
update.plain: routing: mode 0 completes two-token pairs and files them; mode 1 files every symbol under its position before the stop symbol and counts outputs after it; mode 2 files an opener under the raised depth and withdraws the entry at that depth on a closer
update.name: controller

update.latex: \mathrm{ins}(a,b):\; Sq_{en} \leftarrow a,\, Sq_{en+1} \leftarrow b,\, en \leftarrow en+2
update.plain: ins writes the pair at the end of the used part of the strip; a write that would exceed C entries is dropped
update.name: write at end

update.latex: \mathrm{del}(a,b):\; \text{blank the first pair with address } a;\; \text{if it was the last, } en \leftarrow en - 2
update.plain: del blanks the first pair whose address is a and pulls the end back when it was the last
update.name: blank

readout.latex: \mu=0:\; y_0=x_t,\; r_j=\mathrm{get}(y_{j-1}),\; u=r_j \text{ at the first } j\le H \text{ with } r_j\in A,\; u=r_{j-1} \text{ at the first } r_j=\varnothing;\quad \mu=1:\; u=\mathrm{get}(o);\quad \mu=2:\; u=\mathrm{get}(d);\qquad \hat{y}_t = M[u] \text{ for } u\in\mathrm{dom}\,M,\; A_0 \text{ for } u=\varnothing,\; u \text{ otherwise}
readout.plain: output: chase partners from the current token for at most H rounds, stopping at an answer symbol; strings ask for position o, brackets for depth d; translate through M, defaulting to the first answer symbol when nothing is held
readout.name: readout

readout.latex: \mathrm{get}(a):\; hd \leftarrow 0;\; \text{while } hd < en \text{ and } Sq_{hd} \ne a: hd \leftarrow hd + 2;\; \text{return } Sq_{hd+1} \text{ or } \varnothing
readout.plain: get moves the reader from square 0 in steps of two to the first square holding a and returns the square after it

learning.description: Program search over a small space: candidates are (mode, stop symbol) with the stop drawn from the once-per-sequence symbols Z, plus a constant answer. A candidate is scored by running it on the m training sequences and fitting M as the most frequent target for each read result; the top scorer wins.
learning.few_shot_argument: With m = 12 the correct mode and stop symbol are the unique perfect scorers in every small case; M is filled from the same items.

complexity.constants_notes: A scan moves the reader over at most C pairs; at most H scans per token.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Search over a handful of controller settings with a majority translation.

prediction.statement: With m = 12 training examples the learned controller reaches accuracy at least 0.99 on copy at L = 4, recall at K = 4, nesting at depth 2, composition at T = 4 and binding at 2 hops, on three seeds.

capabilities.task: copy a string after a separator
capabilities.prediction: String mode with C = L copies L = 8, 32, 64 over D = 4 with per-string accuracy 1.0 within 2C + N + 16 words.
Pair mode with C = K and H = 1 answers K = 8, 32, 64 with per-query accuracy 1.0 within 2C + N + 16 words (N = 2K + 17 at K = 64 with V = 16).
Nesting mode with C = depth predicts the legal closer at depth 2, 4, 8, 16 with accuracy 1.0 within 2C + N + 16 words.
Pair mode with C = 2T and H = 2 answers f(g(x)) at T = 4, 16, 32 with accuracy 1.0 within 2C + N + 16 words.
Pair mode with C = 2(hops + 1) and H = hops + 1 resolves chains of 1, 4, 8 hops with accuracy 1.0 within 2C + N + 16 words.
The search learner reaches 0.99 from m = 12 examples on seeds 0, 1, 2 for copy at L = 4, recall at K = 4, depth 2, composition at T = 4 and binding at 2 hops.

For any fixed capacity C, recall of K = C + 1 distinct pairs over V = 16 symbols fails on some instance: the store holds at most C pairs, so one probe's item is absent and is answered from at most 16 guesses (at C = 64 this is K = 65, above every P2 size).

toy_example.description: Two pairs written, one fetched, the last one blanked and the end pulled back.
toy_example.python:
import json
Sq = [-1] * 8
en = 0
def ins(a, b):
    global en
    Sq[en] = a; Sq[en + 1] = b; en += 2
def seek(a):
    hd = 0
    while hd < en:
        if Sq[hd] == a:
            return hd
        hd += 2
    return -1
ins(9, 70); ins(4, 71)
got = Sq[seek(4) + 1]
i = seek(4)
Sq[i] = -1; Sq[i + 1] = -1
if i + 2 == en:
    en = i
print(json.dumps({"get4": got, "end": en, "get9": Sq[seek(9) + 1]}))
